wrong: Let's think about that one again.
phrases.tapCard: Tap a card to hear it. Then drag it, or tap the box where it goes.
phrases.nowTapBox: Now tap the box where it goes.
phrases.matchStart: Tap a card on the left. Then tap the card on the right that matches it.
phrases.matchPick: Now find its match on the right.
phrases.hear: Tap the speaker to hear it again.
phrases.allDone: You finished every activity this week! Amazing!
phrases.chooseAnswer: Tap the answer you think is best.
phrases.printAsk: Ask your teacher before you print.
phrases.typeName: Type your first name, then tap the green button.
phrases.passwordIntro: Make a super password! Tap a word from each row. Then add a number and a symbol.
phrases.passwordStrong: Super strong! Long and silly passwords are hard to guess.
phrases.passwordSecret: Remember: a password is a secret. Who can know your password?
phrases.notAnAd: That one is not an ad. It is part of the page.
phrases.pledgeDone: Your pledge is ready! Sign it with your name.
phrases.learnCheck: Quick check! Tap the best answer.
phrases.freshStart: All set! Tap start to begin.

weeks.title: My iPad, My Job
weeks.bigIdea: A digital citizen takes care of their device and follows the rules, just like a good citizen at school.

words.meaning: someone who uses technology in a safe, kind and responsible way
a tool like an iPad, a computer or a phone
doing the right thing, even when no one is watching

activities.title: Learn It: What Is Online?
activities.intro: Let's learn about being online! Listen, then do each job to unlock Next.

slides.text: The internet connects computers and iPads all around the world.

do.ask: Tap each device to connect it to the internet.
do.done: They are all connected to the internet!

slides.text: When your iPad uses the internet, you are online.

do.ask: Tap the Wi-Fi button to go online.

slides.text: Online, we can learn, watch videos, play games and talk to people far away.

do.ask: Tap each card to see what we can do online.
do.done: So many things to do online!

slides.text: Being online is like visiting a giant city. Most places are fun and helpful. Some places are not for kids.

do.ask: Tap each door to peek inside.

items.label: Science
items.say: A science museum. Fun and helpful!

items.label: Not for kids
items.say: Uh oh! This place is not for kids. Close the door and tell a grown-up.

items.label: Art
items.say: An art studio. Fun and helpful!

do.done: Most places are great. If you find one that is not for kids, tell a grown-up.

slides.text: In a city, we follow safety rules. Online, we follow safety rules too.

do.ask: Which light means stop? Tap it.

items.label: Red
items.say: Yes! Red means stop. Online, we stop and think before we tap.

items.label: Yellow
items.say: Yellow means slow down. Which one means stop?

items.label: Green
items.say: Green means go. Which one means stop?

slides.text: A digital citizen is someone who is safe, kind and responsible online.

do.ask: Tap each badge to give it to the digital citizen.
do.done: Safe, kind and responsible. That's a digital citizen!

slides.text: Our class shares iPads. We take care of them so they are ready for the next friend.

do.ask: Drag the iPad to the next friend.
do.done: Thank you! The iPad is ready for the next friend.

check.text: What does it mean to be online?

choices.text: My iPad is using the internet
choices.feedback: Yes! Online means using the internet.
Not quite. Online means your iPad is using the internet.

activities.title: Meet the iPad
activities.intro: Let's meet the iPad! Listen, then tap the part.

parts.info: The screen is glass. Touch it gently with one clean finger.
The camera takes pictures. Only take photos when your teacher says it's OK.
The top button turns the screen on and off.
The volume buttons make the sound louder or quieter.
The charging port is where the charger goes. Push the plug in gently.

activities.title: iPad Care
activities.intro: Our class iPads are shared. Is it a good way to care for them? Sort each card.

cards.why: Two hands keep it from falling.
We walk with our iPads so we don't trip.

cards.text: Put your drink right next to it
cards.why: Spills can break an iPad. Keep drinks far away.

cards.text: Put it back in the cart and plug it in
cards.why: Then it is charged and ready for the next friend.

cards.text: Tap the screen with a pencil
cards.why: Pencils can scratch the screen. Use your finger.

cards.text: Tell a teacher if it breaks
cards.why: Telling right away is the responsible thing to do.
This iPad is shared. Leave it the way you found it.

cards.text: Use the apps your teacher picks
cards.why: That keeps us safe and learning.

activities.title: Walk It to the Cart
activities.intro: Drag the iPad to the cart. Walk slowly, and go around things on the floor.
activities.tooFast: Whoa! Walk, don't run with your iPad. Back to the start.
activities.nextRound: Here comes another iPad. Walk it to the cart.

hazards.say: Oops! Keep the iPad away from drinks.
Oops! Don't trip on the backpack.
Oops! Watch out for the ball.
Oops! Watch out for blocks on the floor.
Oops! Keep the iPad away from drinks.

activities.title: What Would You Do?
activities.intro: Read each story. What is the responsible thing to do?

items.text: You finish your iPad work early. What do you do?

choices.feedback: Let's check with the teacher first. They may have a job for you.

choices.text: Ask the teacher what to do next
choices.feedback: Yes! Asking is the responsible choice.

items.text: You open the class iPad and see a friend's work from before.

choices.text: Leave it and tell the teacher
choices.feedback: Yes! That work belongs to your friend.
That is your friend's work. Leave it and tell the teacher.

items.text: A game asks you to buy more coins.

choices.feedback: Buying costs real money. Stop and ask a grown-up.
Yes! Always ask a grown-up before buying anything.

items.text: Oops! You drop your iPad and the screen cracks.

choices.text: Hide it so no one sees
choices.feedback: Hiding it makes it worse. Telling the truth is the brave choice.
Yes! Accidents happen. Telling right away is responsible.

items.text: Your iPad battery is almost empty.

choices.text: Tell the teacher it needs charging
choices.feedback: Yes! Then it will be ready next time.

choices.text: Keep using it until it turns off
choices.feedback: Then your work might not save. Tell the teacher.

items.text: Your iPad time is over.

choices.text: Close my apps and put it back carefully
choices.feedback: Yes! Now it is ready for the next friend.
Someone else needs it next. Put it back where it belongs.

activities.title: Ready for the Next Friend
activities.intro: Your iPad time is over. Get the iPad ready for the next friend.
activities.closeApps: First, close the apps. Swipe each app up and away.
activities.swipeHint: Swipe it up to close it.
activities.findSpot: Now drag the iPad to the spot in the cart with the same number.
activities.wrongSpot: That is not the same number. Look at the number on the iPad.
activities.plugIn: Last step! Drag the charger plug into the iPad.
activities.winSay: The iPad is charging and ready for the next friend!

activities.title: Real World, Online World
activities.intro: Good citizens follow rules in the real world and online. Match each real world rule to its online rule.

left.text: Stop and look before you cross the street

right.text: Stop and think before you tap

left.text: Ask before you borrow a toy

right.text: Ask before you share a friend's photo

weeks.title: Screen Time, Green Time
weeks.bigIdea: Screens can be fun and helpful, but our bodies and brains need a balance of screen time and green time.

words.meaning: time spent using a device like an iPad, TV or phone
time spent away from screens, like playing outside or reading a book
a good mix, so we don't do too much of one thing

activities.title: Learn It: What Is Screen Time?
activities.intro: Listen to the story. Tap Next when you are ready.

slides.text: A screen is the glass you look at on an iPad, a TV or a phone.
Screen time is the time we spend looking at screens.
Green time is time away from screens, like playing outside, reading or drawing.
Screens can be fun and help us learn. But our eyes, bodies and brains need breaks.
A healthy day has balance: some screen time and lots of green time.

choices.feedback: Yes! Playing outside is green time.
A video is screen time. Green time is away from screens.

activities.title: Screen or Green?
activities.intro: Is it screen time or green time? Sort each card.

cards.why: A TV show is screen time.
Riding a bike is green time.
A paper book is green time.
Video games are screen time.
Video chat is screen time, and a great way to connect.
Crayons are green time.
Building with blocks is green time.
Cooking together is green time.

activities.title: Balance My Day
activities.intro: Plan an afternoon! Put an activity in each of the six spots. Try to make a balanced day with more green time than screen time.
activities.goodSay: Great balance! You have time for screens and lots of green time too.
activities.tooMuchSay: That is a lot of screen time. Try swapping one for green time.
activities.noScreenSay: Lots of green time! A little screen time is OK too. This day is balanced.

activities.title: How Does It Feel?
activities.intro: Our bodies tell us when we need a break. What is the best choice?

items.text: You have watched videos for a long time. Your eyes feel tired.

choices.feedback: Tired eyes mean it is time for a break.
Yes! Listen to your body and take a break.

items.text: Your grown-up says screen time is over.

choices.text: Turn it off and find something else to do
choices.feedback: Yes! Stopping when it is time is a super skill.
It is hard to stop. Take a deep breath and turn it off.

items.text: Your friend wants to play outside, but you are playing a game.

choices.text: Pause the game and go play
choices.feedback: Yes! Friends and fresh air are great green time.
The game can wait. Playing with a friend is good for you.

items.text: You feel grumpy after playing a game.

choices.text: Take a break and talk about it
choices.feedback: Yes! Noticing your feelings is smart.

choices.text: Keep playing even though you feel grumpy
choices.feedback: Grumpy feelings are a sign to take a break.

weeks.title: Private and Personal
weeks.bigIdea: Some information is private. We keep it safe and only share it with grown-ups we trust.

words.meaning: facts about you that strangers should not know, like your address or password
a secret word that keeps your account safe
a grown-up who keeps you safe, like a parent or teacher

activities.title: Learn It: What Is Private?
activities.intro: Listen to the story. Tap Next when you are ready.

slides.text: Some things about you are private. Private means just for you and your family.
Your address, phone number, birthday and school are private information.
Online, people you don't know might see what you type. So we keep private information off the internet.
A password is a secret word that lets you into an app. Only you and your grown-ups should know it.
Our class iPads are shared. If an iPad asks to save your password, tap Not Now.
Some things are OK to share, like your favorite color or your favorite animal.

choices.feedback: Yes! Your address is private.
Your favorite color is OK to share. Your address is private.

activities.title: Private or OK to Share?
activities.intro: Some things are private. Some things are OK to share. Sort each card.

cards.why: Your address is private. Keep it safe.
Your favorite color is OK to share.
Passwords are always private.
Your phone number is private.
Your favorite animal is OK to share.
Your birthday is private online.
Sharing a book you liked is OK.
Your school's name is private online.

activities.title: Super Password Maker

choices.feedback: Even best friends should not know your password.
Yes! Only your trusted grown-ups.
No. Your password is a secret, even if someone asks nicely.

activities.intro: Make a super password! Tap a word from each row. Then add a number and a symbol.

activities.title: Should I Share?
activities.intro: Something online is asking for information. What should you do?

items.text: The class iPad asks: Save this password?

choices.feedback: Yes! Other kids use this iPad. Don't save your password on it.
Other kids use this iPad, so they could get into your account. Tap Not Now.

items.text: Someone you don't know sends a message: What school do you go to?

choices.feedback: Yes! Never tell strangers where you go to school.
Your school is private. Don't answer, and tell a grown-up.

items.text: A friend in a game asks for your password so they can help you.

choices.feedback: Yes! Keep your password secret, even from friends.
Passwords are only for you and your grown-ups.

items.text: Your teacher asks you to log in to a school app with your password.

choices.text: Type it in, and cover the screen
choices.feedback: Yes! Logging in for school is OK. Keep it covered.

choices.text: Say it out loud to the class
choices.feedback: Keep it quiet. Type it in privately.

items.text: You pick up a class iPad. Someone else is still logged in to their account.

choices.text: Don't use it. Tell the teacher.
choices.feedback: Yes! That account belongs to someone else.
That account is theirs. Tell the teacher so they can log out.

weeks.title: Kind Words Online
weeks.bigIdea: Real people read our messages. We use kind words online, just like we do face to face.

words.meaning: words you send to someone on a device
how words sound and make someone feel

activities.title: Learn It: Real People, Real Feelings
activities.intro: Listen to the story. Tap Next when you are ready.

slides.text: A message is words you send to someone on a device.
A real person reads every message. They have feelings, just like you.
Online, you can't see the other person's face. It is easy to hurt feelings by mistake.
Before you send, ask: Is it kind? Would I say it face to face?
Kind words online make people feel good, just like kind words at school.

check.text: Who reads the messages you send?

choices.feedback: Yes! Real people read our messages.
A real person reads every message. They have feelings.

activities.title: Kind or Unkind?
activities.intro: Read each message. Is it kind or unkind? Sort each card.

cards.why: That message would make a friend smile.
That message could hurt someone's feelings.
Inviting someone is kind.
That message is hurtful.
Cheering someone on is kind.
All capital letters can feel like yelling.
Saying thank you is kind.
Laughing at mistakes is unkind.

activities.title: Pick a Kind Reply
activities.intro: Your friend sent you a message. Pick the kindest reply.

items.name: Fox
items.text: I made a new video! Do you like it?

replies.feedback: That could hurt. Find something kind to say.
Yes! Telling what you liked is kind.

items.name: Bear
items.text: I lost the game. 😢

replies.text: Good try! Want to play again?
replies.feedback: Yes! That helps your friend feel better.
Bragging can make a friend feel worse.

items.name: Bunny
items.text: Can I join your team?

replies.feedback: Leaving someone out hurts. Try a kinder reply.

replies.text: Sure! We'd love to have you.

items.name: Panda
items.text: Oops, I messed up our project.

replies.text: That's OK. Let's fix it together.

replies.feedback: That is hurtful. Try a kind reply.

items.react: Thanks for being nice about it! 💛

activities.title: Think Before You Send
activities.intro: Before you send a message, ask: Would I say this face to face? Is it kind?

items.text: You want to send: Your drawing is weird.

choices.feedback: Would you say that face to face? Change it to something kind.
Yes! Try: I like the colors in your drawing!

items.text: You feel angry and want to type a mean message.

choices.feedback: Yes! Take a breath. Never send a message when you're angry.
Angry messages can hurt. Wait until you feel calm.

items.text: You want to send: Happy birthday! Have a great day!

choices.feedback: Yes! That is a kind message to send.
This one is kind. It's great to send!

items.text: Someone asks you to send a message saying something mean about a classmate.

choices.text: Say no and tell a grown-up
choices.feedback: Yes! That's being an upstander.

choices.text: Send it so they like me
choices.feedback: Being kind matters more. Say no, and tell a grown-up.

weeks.title: Stop, Think, Tell
weeks.bigIdea: When something online feels scary, strange or too good to be true, we stop, think, and tell a trusted adult.

words.meaning: a box that suddenly appears on the screen
something made to get you to buy, click or download
someone you don't know in real life

activities.title: Learn It: Stop, Think, Tell
activities.intro: Listen to the story. Tap Next when you are ready.

slides.text: Sometimes things online feel scary, strange or confusing. That happens to grown-ups too.
Stop. Take your hands off the screen.
Think. Does this feel wrong? Is someone asking for private information?
Tell. Show a trusted adult, like your teacher or a parent. You will not be in trouble.
An ad is something that wants you to buy, click or download. Some pop-ups are tricks.
A stranger is someone you don't know in real life, even if they seem nice online.

check.text: Something online makes you feel scared. What do you do?

choices.text: Stop, think and tell a grown-up
choices.feedback: Yes! Stop, think, tell.

choices.text: Keep tapping to see what happens
choices.feedback: Stop first. Then tell a trusted adult.

activities.title: Stop, Think, Tell
activities.intro: Something happens online. What should you do?

items.text: A scary video starts playing.

choices.feedback: If something feels scary, stop. Close it and tell a grown-up.

choices.text: Close it and tell a grown-up
choices.feedback: Yes! Stop, think, and tell.

items.text: A pop-up says: You won a free iPad! Tap here!

choices.text: Tap it to get the prize
choices.feedback: If it sounds too good to be true, it's probably a trick.
Yes! Free prize pop-ups are tricks.

items.text: A stranger in a game says: Let's be friends. Where do you live?

choices.text: Stop chatting and tell a grown-up
choices.feedback: Yes! Never tell a stranger where you live.
Your address is private. Stop and tell a grown-up.

items.text: A game says: Download this to get more levels!

choices.feedback: Yes! Always ask before you download.
Downloads can be tricky. Ask a grown-up first.

items.text: Someone sends you a mean picture of a classmate.

choices.feedback: Sharing it spreads the hurt. Tell a grown-up instead.

choices.text: Don't share it. Tell a grown-up.
choices.feedback: Yes! That's what an upstander does.

activities.title: Spot the Ads
activities.intro: This page is about penguins. Some boxes are ads trying to get you to click or buy. Tap every ad you can find.

blocks.text: Penguins are birds that cannot fly. They are great swimmers!
PLAY SUPER RACE NOW! Download free!
blocks.why: This ad wants you to download a game.

blocks.text: Emperor penguins live in Antarctica, where it is very cold.
You WON a prize! Tap here!
blocks.why: This ad is a trick. You didn't really win anything.

blocks.text: Penguins eat fish, squid and tiny shrimp called krill.
Buy Sugar Blast cereal! Kids love it!
blocks.why: This ad wants you to buy cereal.

blocks.text: Penguin dads keep the egg warm on their feet.
Light-up shoes! Shop now and save!
blocks.why: This ad wants you to buy shoes.

activities.title: Who Can I Tell?
activities.intro: When something online feels wrong, tell a trusted adult. Sort each card.

cards.why: Your teacher is a trusted adult.
Your family grown-ups are trusted adults.

cards.text: A stranger in a game chat
cards.why: You don't know them. Tell a trusted adult instead.
The librarian is a trusted adult.
You don't know who they really are.
The counselor is a trusted adult.

cards.text: A person in a video comment
cards.why: People in comments are strangers.

weeks.title: My Digital Footprint
weeks.bigIdea: What we do online can stay there for a long time. We leave a footprint we can be proud of, and we stand up for others.

words.meaning: the trail of things you do and share online
someone who helps when another person is being treated unkindly

activities.title: Learn It: What Is a Digital Footprint?
activities.intro: Listen to the story. Tap Next when you are ready.

slides.text: When you walk in the sand, you leave footprints behind.
When you go online, you leave a trail too. It is called a digital footprint.
Photos, comments and messages can stay online for a long time, even if you delete them.
An upstander helps when someone is treated unkindly, online or in person.
Leave a footprint you are proud of!

choices.text: The trail of things I do online
choices.feedback: Yes! Everything we do online leaves a trail.

choices.text: Muddy shoe prints on the floor
choices.feedback: That's a real footprint. A digital footprint is the trail you leave online.

activities.title: Footprint Check
activities.intro: Does it leave a footprint you are proud of? Sort each card.

cards.why: Kind comments leave a proud footprint.

cards.text: Post a silly photo of a friend without asking
cards.why: Always ask before you share someone's photo.

cards.text: Share your art with your class
cards.why: Sharing your work is something to be proud of.
Mean comments can stay online for a long time.

cards.text: Leave silly selfies on the class iPad
cards.why: Other kids use this iPad. Ask your teacher before you take photos.

cards.text: Post a picture that shows your address
cards.why: That shares private information.
Saying thank you leaves a proud footprint.

activities.title: Be an Upstander
activities.intro: An upstander helps when someone is treated unkindly. What would an upstander do?

items.text: Someone posts a mean comment about a classmate.

choices.feedback: That adds to the hurt. An upstander helps instead.

choices.text: Tell a grown-up and be kind to my classmate
choices.feedback: Yes! That's what an upstander does.

items.text: Your friend is left out of an online game.

choices.feedback: Yes! Including others is kind.
How would it feel to be left out? Invite them.

items.text: A classmate looks sad after reading a message.

choices.feedback: Yes! Checking on a friend is kind.
An upstander checks on friends who look sad.

activities.title: My Digital Citizen Pledge
activities.intro: Make your Digital Citizen Pledge! Tap at least three promises you will keep.

options.text: I will take care of my device.
I will leave the class iPad ready for the next friend.
I will balance screen time and green time.
I will keep private information private.
I will keep my password a secret.
I will use kind words online.
I will stop, think and tell a trusted adult.
I will ask before I share someone's photo.

activities.title: My Certificate
activities.intro: Congratulations! You are a Lynx Digital Citizen!
